## Subtract a negative index {#combine}

Expand the numerator. When a denominator index is negative, put it in brackets before subtracting.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$\dfrac{(2a^{-1}b^3)^2}{8a^2b^{-1}}$

::: {.fragment}

[Square each factor.]{.annotation}

$=\dfrac{4a^{-2}b^6}{8a^2b^{-1}}$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Subtract the denominator indices.]{.annotation}

$=\dfrac{1}{2}a^{-2-2}b^{6-(-1)}$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Finish with positive indices.]{.annotation}

$=\dfrac{1}{2}a^{-4}b^7=\dfrac{b^7}{2a^4}$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$\dfrac{(3x^{-1}y^2)^2}{6x^2y^{-1}}$

Try it on paper, then select **Next** to check.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$=\dfrac{9x^{-2}y^4}{6x^2y^{-1}}$

$=\dfrac{3}{2}x^{-4}y^{4-(-1)}=\dfrac{3y^5}{2x^4}$

:::
